## Assembly Structure and Officers
The Assembly has 31 elected Delegates. The Speaker of Benches presides and votes only to break ties. The Clerk of the Roll keeps the Ledger of Bills, and the Provost of Finance certifies any bill that spends money from the Activity Chest.
A quorum is 20 Delegates present. If a quorum call fails twice in one session, the Speaker must adjourn. Any Delegate may introduce a bill by filing three typed copies with the Clerk before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday. Each bill gets a number with the prefix 'BA' and the session year.
Every bill needs a Sponsor and at least two Seconders. The Clerk reads the title aloud at the first session after filing; this is the First Reading, with no debate. The Speaker refers each bill to one of four standing committees. A bill spending more than 40 Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Key: 31 Delegates; Speaker votes only to break ties.
Key: Quorum is 20; two failed quorum calls force adjournment.
Key: Bills filed with Clerk before 8:15 a.m. Tuesday, three copies, numbered BA-year.
Key: Sponsor plus two Seconders; First Reading is title only, no debate.
Key: Committees: Grounds (7), Clubs (7), Chest (9), Rules (8); >40 Silver Marks → Chest.
Q: How many Delegates make up the Assembly? A: 31. The passage states the Assembly consists of thirty-one elected Delegates.
Q: When may the Speaker of Benches vote on a bill? A: Only to break a tie. The passage says the Speaker may vote only to break ties.
Q: A bill that spends 50 Silver Marks must be referred to which committee? A: Committee on the Chest. The passage says a bill spending more than 40 Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Q: If a quorum call fails twice in one session, what must the Speaker do? A: Adjourn. The passage states the Speaker must adjourn after two failed quorum calls.
Q: A Delegate wants to introduce a bill. What must they file with the Clerk of the Roll? A: Three typed copies. The passage says filing three typed copies is required.
Q: What happens at the First Reading of a bill? A: The Clerk reads the title aloud. The passage says the Clerk reads the title aloud and no debate occurs.
Q: What is the minimum number of Seconders a bill must have? A: two (2). The passage states every bill must have at least two Seconders.
Q: What prefix must a bill number carry? A: BA. The passage says each bill number begins with the prefix 'BA'.
Q: If a bill spends 45 Silver Marks, which committee must it go to? A: Committee on the Chest. The passage says bills spending more than 40 Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.

## Introducing a Bill
To introduce a bill in the Brookhaven Academy Student Assembly, any Delegate must file three typed copies with the Clerk of the Roll before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday. The Clerk assigns each bill a number with the prefix 'BA' followed by the session year, like BA-24-07.
Every bill must have a Sponsor and at least two Seconders. After filing, the Clerk reads the title aloud at the first session after filing; this is the First Reading, and no debate occurs at that time.
The Speaker then refers the bill to one of four standing committees. A bill that spends more than forty Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.
Key: File 3 typed copies before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday.
Key: Bill number: BA + session year (e.g., BA-24-07).
Key: Need a Sponsor and at least 2 Seconders.
Key: First Reading: title read aloud, no debate.
Key: Spending >40 Silver Marks → Committee on the Chest.
Q: How many typed copies of a bill must a Delegate file with the Clerk of the Roll? A: Three. Section 3 states 'filing three (3) typed copies with the Clerk of the Roll'.
Q: What is the deadline for filing a bill? A: Before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday. Section 3 says 'before 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday'.
Q: A bill is assigned the number BA-24-07. What does '24' represent? A: The session year. Section 3 says the prefix 'BA' followed by the session year, e.g., BA-24-07.
Q: What happens at the First Reading of a bill? A: The Clerk reads the title aloud, and no debate occurs. Section 4 says 'The Clerk reads the title aloud at the first session after filing; this is the First Reading. No debate occurs at the First Reading.'
Q: A bill that spends 45 Silver Marks must be referred to which committee? A: Committee on the Chest. Section 5 says 'A bill that spends more than forty (40) Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.'
Q: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for introducing a bill? A: Getting approval from the Provost of Finance. Section 3 and 4 list the requirements: three copies, a Sponsor, and at least two Seconders. The Provost of Finance only certifies bills that spend money, not all bills.
Q: What is the minimum number of Seconders required for a bill? A: two. Section 4 says 'at least two (2) Seconders'.
Q: What is the name of the officer who assigns numbers to bills? A: Clerk of the Roll. Section 3 says 'Each bill must carry a number assigned by the Clerk' and Section 1 names the Clerk of the Roll.
Q: If a bill spends 40 Silver Marks exactly, must it go to the Committee on the Chest? A: No. The rule applies only to bills that spend 'more than forty (40) Silver Marks', so exactly 40 does not trigger it.

## Committee Review
When a bill is introduced, the Speaker refers it to one of four standing committees based on its subject and cost. A bill that spends more than forty Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest. Committees meet on Thursdays, and a committee quorum is five members. The committee can report the bill favorably, report it with amendments, table it, or kill it by a two-thirds vote of members present.
After a committee reports a bill, it receives its Second Reading no sooner than three school days later. At the Second Reading, the Clerk reads the full text, and delegates may speak. Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote. The Third Reading happens right after amendments are settled, and passage requires a simple majority of delegates present, but never fewer than eleven yes votes.
A key rule is that no bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, unless all Delegates present give unanimous consent. This means the final vote cannot happen on the same day as the Second Reading unless every Delegate present agrees to allow it.
Key: No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.
Key: Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.
Q: What is the minimum number of Delegates that must be present for a quorum in the Assembly? A: 20. Section 2 states: 'A quorum is twenty (20) Delegates present in the Chamber.'
Q: A bill that spends 50 Silver Marks must be referred to which committee? A: Committee on the Chest. Section 5 says: 'A bill that spends more than forty (40) Silver Marks must go to the Committee on the Chest.'
Q: What is the committee quorum? A: 5. Section 6 states: 'A committee quorum is five (5).'
Q: A bill receives its Second Reading on Monday. When can it be voted on? A: Monday, if all Delegates present agree. Section 9 says: 'No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.' So it can be voted on the same day only with unanimous consent.
Q: How are amendments voted on? A: By show of hands, individually. Section 8 says: 'Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.'
Q: A bill is reported out of committee on Thursday. What is the earliest day it can receive its Second Reading? A: The next Tuesday. Section 7 says: 'A bill reported out of committee receives its Second Reading no sooner than three (3) school days later.' If reported on Thursday, the next school days are Friday, Monday, Tuesday, so Tuesday is the earliest.
Q: What is the minimum number of yes votes needed for a bill to pass? A: 11. Section 8 says: 'Passage requires an affirmative vote of a simple majority of Delegates present, but never fewer than eleven (11) yes votes.'
Q: A bill receives its Second Reading on Wednesday. The Speaker calls for a vote the same day. What must happen for the vote to be allowed? A: All Delegates present must consent. Section 9 says: 'No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.'
Q: What is the maximum number of times the Sponsor may speak during the Second Reading? A: twice. Section 7 says: 'the Sponsor may speak twice.'

## Floor Debate and Voting
A bill reported out of committee gets its Second Reading no sooner than three school days later. The Clerk reads the full text, and each Delegate may speak once for up to four minutes, except the Sponsor who may speak twice.
Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote. After amendments are settled, the Third Reading occurs immediately. Passage requires a simple majority of Delegates present, but never fewer than eleven yes votes.
No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present. This rule prevents same-day passage unless every Delegate agrees.
After passage, the Chancellor has five school days to sign the bill (making it an Act), veto it with a written objection of no more than 150 words, or return it unsigned after five days, in which case it becomes an Act without signature.
Key: No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.
Key: Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.
Q: What is the general rule about voting on a bill on the same day it receives its Second Reading? A: It is prohibited unless all Delegates present consent unanimously.. Section 9 states the rule clearly.
Q: How are amendments voted on? A: Individually by show of hands.. Section 8 specifies the method.
Q: A bill receives its Second Reading on Monday. When is the earliest it can be voted on, assuming no unanimous consent? A: Thursday.. Section 7 says no sooner than three school days later, and Section 9 prohibits same-day vote.
Q: If 20 Delegates are present, what is the minimum number of yes votes needed for passage? A: 11. Section 8 requires a simple majority but never fewer than 11.
Q: What happens if the Chancellor does nothing with a passed bill for five school days? A: The bill becomes an Act without signature.. Section 10(c) states it becomes an Act without signature.
Q: What is the maximum number of words allowed in a veto message? A: 150. Section 10(b) specifies the limit.
Q: A bill is reported out of committee on a Friday. What is the earliest school day it can receive its Second Reading? A: Wednesday. Section 7 requires three school days later; Friday to Monday is one, Tuesday is two, Wednesday is three.
Q: During the Second Reading, how many times may the Sponsor speak? A: Twice. Section 7 says the Sponsor may speak twice.
Q: What fraction of committee members must vote to kill a bill? A: two-thirds. Section 6(d) states the requirement.

## Executive Action and Veto
The Chancellor, elected at large, is the Assembly's presiding executive. Within five school days of a bill's passage, the Chancellor must either sign it (making it an Act, entered in the Ledger with a seal), veto it with a written objection of no more than 150 words, or return it unsigned after five days, in which case it becomes an Act without signature.
A vetoed bill returns to the floor at the next session. The Assembly may override the veto only by a vote of twenty-one of the thirty-one Delegates. If the override succeeds, the bill becomes an Act over the Chancellor's objection.
No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present. This rule ensures a waiting period before the final vote.
Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote. The Third Reading occurs immediately after amendments are settled. Passage requires an affirmative vote of a simple majority of Delegates present, but never fewer than eleven yes votes.
Key: No bill may be voted on the same day it receives its Second Reading, except by unanimous consent of all Delegates present.
Key: Amendments are voted on individually by show of hands before the final vote.

Q: A bill passes with 12 yes votes and 5 no votes. Is this sufficient for passage? A: Yes, because it is a simple majority.. Passage requires a simple majority of Delegates present, but never fewer than 11 yes votes. 12 meets both.
Q: The Chancellor vetoes a bill. What happens next? A: The bill returns to the floor at the next session and can be overridden by 21 votes.. The passage describes the veto process.

Q: How many votes are needed to override a veto? A: twenty-one. The passage specifies the number.
Q: A bill receives its Second Reading on Tuesday. The Sponsor wants a vote on Wednesday. Can this happen? A: Yes, if all Delegates present consent unanimously.. The rule prohibits voting on the same day as Second Reading, but allows it with unanimous consent.

## Effective Dates and Publication
A vetoed bill returns to the floor at the next session. The Assembly can override the veto with 21 of 31 Delegates, making it an Act despite the Chancellor's objection.
An Act takes effect at 8:00 a.m. on the 10th school day after signature, unless it states a later date. Acts affecting the Activity Chest need the Provost of Finance's countersign to take effect.
The Clerk of the Roll must publish every Act on the Assembly board within 2 school days of effect. If not published in time, the Act is suspended until publication.
Repealing an Act follows the same process as enacting, but the committee stage can be waived by a two-thirds floor vote. Emergency measures for health or safety can be introduced anytime and passed by 24 Delegates, but expire after 20 school days unless re-enacted normally.

Key: Activity Chest acts need Provost of Finance countersign
Key: Publication within 2 school days of effect, else suspended
Key: Repeal: same path, committee waiver by 2/3 vote
Key: Emergency: 24 votes, expires in 20 school days
